x: Jim Beer, now in India, has been doing some racing and gained a third in both the half and one mile. He was chasing Manley, of Woodford Green.

The next two men home were Miles and Manley, also of Thames Valley, and so they scored a hollow victory in the team race. We were pleased to hear that we had been awarded second place after a tie with Portsmouth A.C., our third scoring man being placed nearer than theirs.

Len Herbert then exceeded our wildest hopes by not only catching his rival, but giving us a lead of 24 seconds, and Archie Bedford ran a gallant race to keep the lead, although Manley, of T.V.H., gained on him a little.
